messages:
eng-bot: :rotating_light: Incident pager: possible presigned-url exposure triggered for service 'file-proxy' at 2024-12-05T18:02:42Z. Severity P1 - automatic page.
Alice (oncall): acked, jumping in. pulling logs now.
Ben SRE: I'm seeing a spike in presigned URL issuance from a cron job between 18:00-18:07 UTC. counts: ~3200 tokens issued, 0 errors on issuance.
Alice (oncall): any signs of external access using those URLs?
Ben SRE: quick grep shows ~12 successful GETs from IPs we don't recognize, timestamps within that 7m window. investigating paths now.
Dmitri Eng: hypothesis: recent deploy of the presign TTL change allowed URLs to be longer-lived than intended (24h vs 15m). config drift in deploy-meta.
Carla Privacy: :warning: Important — need to confirm whether any payloads delivered contain PII. If logs or user content were downloaded we may have to notify.
Alice (oncall): safe plan: (1) revoke all presigned tokens generated in the window, (2) roll back the TTL change, (3) snapshot evidence and scope, (4) draft customer notice if scope includes customer content. Doing 1 now.
Ben SRE: running revoke script against token-issuance-index for epoch range.```bash
# revoke presigned tokens between 1700000000 and 1700000420
python ops/revoke_presigned.py --from 1700000000 --to 1700000420 --service file-proxy
```
eng-bot: Revoke job queued: job-id 61c2f7. Estimated completion 00:00:30.
Ben SRE: revoke job succeeded. confirmed 3,200 tokens invalidated.
Dmitri Eng: rolling back config to previous tag now and redeploying. ETA ~8m.
Alice (oncall): Carla - quick ask: can you triage sample of the 12 IP GETs and check returned objects for PII? I'll capture full request/response headers.
Carla Privacy: on it. Pulling response snapshots. initial pass: 8 of 12 responses were metadata-only, 4 contained user-uploaded text blobs. Need content inspection.
Sam CS: flagging CS standby in case we need to notify customers — who would be affected? any account ids?
Ben SRE: scanning logs for account_id headers in those 4 downloads.```text
found account_ids: acct_203, acct_441, acct_203, acct_789
```
Alice (oncall): acct_203 appears twice. priority: acct_203, acct_441, acct_789.
Carla Privacy: manual review of blob contents: acct_203 blob A contains an email + partial address. acct_441 content appears to be internal logs (no user data). acct_789 blob is an image with no visible metadata.
Carla Privacy: conclusion: potential exposure of PII for acct_203. We should prepare a targeted customer notification for acct_203 and a general status page notice.
Dmitri Eng: we should also check object versioning: whether the downloaded object is the latest or an older version. If older, scope might be different.
Alice (oncall): next steps checklist in-thread:
- [x] revoke tokens in-window
- [x] rollback TTL deploy
- [x] collect evidence (request/response snapshots)
- [ ] validate list of impacted accounts + assets (Carla)
- [ ] draft customer notice (Sam + Olivia)
- [ ] review with Legal for regulator requirements (Olivia)
- [ ] publish short status page update (Alice)
- [ ] schedule handoff to next oncall (Maria)
Carla Privacy: impact table (quick):```text
acct_203: 1 object (text blob), contains email and partial address -> likely PII
acct_441: 1 object (internal logs) -> no customer PII
acct_789: 1 object (image) -> no PII seen
```
Olivia Legal: I can review the draft notice. Need to know whether this crosses breach disclosure thresholds in applicable jurisdictions. For now treat as 'potential unauthorized access' to customer data for acct_203.
Sam CS: drafting customer notice for acct_203 now. Will post draft below for review. Also prepping templated FAQ and support playbook.
Sam CS: DRAFT (for acct_203):
```
Hi <Customer Contact>,

We are contacting you about a potential unauthorized access to an object in your Redwood account (acct_203) on 2024-12-05 between 18:00 and 18:07 UTC. We identified a short-lived presigned URL issuance bug that may have allowed external access to one object.

What happened: a recent configuration change caused presigned URLs to be issued with longer TTLs than intended. We revoked the affected tokens and rolled back the change.

What data may have been affected: a single uploaded text file that appears to contain an email address and partial mailing address.

Our actions: revoked tokens, rolled back the change, rotated related service keys, and are completing a forensic review. We will update you with any new findings.

Recommended customer actions: please rotate any credentials contained in the affected file and contact support if you need assistance.

We apologize for the inconvenience. If you'd like a call to review, reply and we'll schedule.

Regards,
Redwood Security Team
```
Olivia Legal: initial feedback: language is OK but add timeframe for follow-up (e.g., 72 hours), remove implication of confirmed unauthorized access — use "potential unauthorized access" as you have. Add contact for data protection officer if they request. Also we should avoid instructing customers to rotate credentials if we haven't confirmed credentials in the file — instead suggest 'consider rotating'.
Sam CS: updating draft per Legal. New DRAFT posted.
Dmitri Eng: ops question — we've rotated service keys? Alice, please confirm rotation command ran.
Alice (oncall): rotating service keys and pushing rotation to vault now.```bash
vault write secret/file-proxy/keys value=$(generate-key)
kubectl rollout restart deployment/file-proxy
```
Alice (oncall): rotation complete. verified no queued presign events after rotation.
eng-bot: Deploy event: rollback->file-proxy v1.4.3 succeeded at 18:12:05 UTC.
Alice (oncall): status page copy suggestion (short, non-technical):
```
At 18:00 UTC on 2024-12-05 we detected a short-lived configuration issue affecting presigned URL expiry for our file proxy service. We have revoked the affected URLs, rolled back the change, and completed a targeted review. We are contacting any customers with potentially affected content directly.
```
Carla Privacy: recommend adding "no evidence of widespread access" if that's accurate after review.
Alice (oncall): good call. updated status copy to add that.
Sam CS: putting together customer email list and finalizing acct_203 notification. Will send once Olivia gives final legal signoff.
Olivia Legal: signoff pending small edits — add 72h follow-up and DPO contact. Once Sam posts final, I’ll stamp.
Ben SRE: quick ask for FYI: we should add a test in the presign CI to detect TTL drift. I opened PR #492 for that.
Dmitri Eng: will prioritize test and gating in CI.
Alice (oncall): handoff: Maria, I'll brief you on the timeline and outstanding items. Key things for next oncall: monitor for any new access attempts, confirm final legal-approved customer notice sent, follow up on forensic timeline.
Maria (next-oncall): acked, I'll take over at 19:00 UTC. Please drop any runbook links and playbooks into this thread.
Alice (oncall): runbook excerpt: https://confluence/internal/runbooks/presign-incident - section 'revocation' and 'evidence collection'.
Carla Privacy: final note: we'll prepare an internal escalation memo for compliance and, if needed, regulator notification. For now controlled scope: one customer with possible PII exposure.
Alice (oncall): filing incident ticket INC-2024-447 with summary and timeline. We'll update status page in 30 minutes with the copy above and send customer notice once legal signs off.
Sam CS: final send plan: send to acct_203 via primary email and Slack contact, include attachment with forensic summary.
Olivia Legal: stamped. Sam, you can send.
Sam CS: sent to acct_203 at 18:44 UTC. copy of sent message posted to helpdesk ticket.
Alice (oncall): great work team. I'll leave the thread open for any new findings. Maria, please post closure summary when done. :thumbsup:
